playbook:
When a pledge is required, I only pledge missions I can and will perform — I never pledge raid/escort unless I will pay that fuel and perform that act at the act stage.

When my pledged move would leave me with zero or negative fuel before later rounds, I choose scout instead (preserve fuel and avoid negative final-score penalties).

When I pledge escort, I act escort (do not switch to scout) to actually block incoming raids and secure the 2 points.

When I pledge raid, I act raid — only if the clockwise target is likely scouting and has points to steal, and only if I can afford the fuel cost without forcing negative fuel later.

When two opponents are repeatedly scouting and I can afford it, I prefer raid (to capitalize on unprotected scouts), but only if the raid will not produce negative fuel.

When I expect an opponent to raid me (based on their prior pattern or leadership), I pledge escort to deny their theft — escort to escort, not escort then scout.

When both opponents show mixed scout/raid tendencies and I need steady points, I pledge scout to safely score 3 unless I’m being targeted by a predictable raid.

When I have very low fuel late in the game, I prioritize scouting to bank points and unused-fuel opportunities over risky pledges that I can’t actually perform.

If majority of players publicly pledge scout, I still consider raiding only if I can perform it and the clockwise target is likely vulnerable; otherwise match the majority with scout to conserve fuel.

Never change my act from my recorded pledge — that produced contradictions and penalties; always ensure pledge = act.

If behind on points and able to pay, pick calculated raids only when the target has points to steal and when the raid’s expected net gain exceeds the risk of being countered (escort/raid cost to me).

If ahead and with modest fuel, favor escort or scout to preserve lead and avoid being exploited by desperate raiders.
